upstream_source.scope: Windows post-relaunch wait and old process incarnation only; N52 maps process classification and N54 maps test-only spawn admission.

contract: A mapped Windows Gateway relaunch is verified only after its original (pid, create_time) incarnation is no longer live and a fresh fleet snapshot is read. The bounded wait covers the detached watcher's 120-second deadline plus 30 seconds while that incarnation is pending. PID reuse, unreadable identity, a stale row, and strict discovery failure cannot authorize a replacement claim. Verified siblings retain restart eligibility.
source_and_caller: hermes_cli/gateway.py:_spawn_gateway_restart_watcher waits for the old incarnation and declines a second launch if it remains live at the deadline.

hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:_pause_windows_gateways_for_update captures strict identities, _resume_windows_gateways_after_update passes them to mapped watchers, and _poll_fleet_versions_with_relaunch_budget retries if the old incarnation exits during collection.
gateway/status.py:_pid_identity_is_live distinguishes PID reuse and treats unreadable identity as pending; generic manual profile and command-line fallback callers propagate this identity.

evidence.red: The prior isolated N53 work recorded sequential RED for wait budget, stale snapshot, generic caller, unreadable identity, and per-profile isolation. The stacked independent review found that a successfully armed mapped watcher could bypass fleet verification when earlier inventory and PID snapshot were empty. A new regression test failed against that actual source: _fleet_probe_expected_runtimes returned False despite watcher_old_identities.
evidence.green: On the initial stacked product, five safe Windows-focused modules passed 89/89 and Gateway status/holder caller tests separately passed 98/98 with 18 dependency deprecation warnings. After the P2 correction, seven focused modules passed 109/109; the downstream Windows fleet-kind contract separately passed 3/3. Ruff on the corrected paths and staged diff check passed. No real Gateway was launched by these selected tests.
evidence.mutation: Four controlled mutants were killed on the prior local N53 candidate 724beb34742f71b5327b61f63b3874f1591a235b; their results are historical because this integration contains N52 reaper work. The observed pre-correction fleet gate was an additional live counterexample killed by the new test.
evidence.codegraph: Approved CodeGraph 1.6.0 synced the five initial changed files, then three post-review changes, in the actual integration index. Final post-edit status reported 8,922 files and no pending changes. Query found _fleet_probe_expected_runtimes at update_cmd.py:10689; impact reached _cmd_update_impl and relevant regression tests. Explore and affected ran; broad unrelated results were discounted in favor of actual source/caller inspection.
evidence.independent_review: Boole independently reviewed the final stacked source and regression test, verified their SHA256 bindings, and reported CLEAR for the corrected fleet gate and caller. Laplace's separate review is still pending; prior Kepler and Code Reviewer CLEAR applied to the previous local candidate only.

open_gaps: Token-only or unmapped watcher replacements do not have destination outcome durability evidence. This bounded result does not prove whole U1 parity, live fleet health, or release readiness.
